Hey there @hfurubotten, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`entur_public_transport`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L327) for? Thanks!

> Hei, I wanted to try this out, but I'm only getting the following error when configuring Entur from your branch:
> 
> ```
>   File "/Users/vs/git/core/homeassistant/components/entur_public_transport/sensor.py", line 27, in <module>
>     API_CLIENT_NAME = "homeassistant-{}".format(Context(user_id=user.id))
> NameError: name 'user' is not defined
> ```

Not surprising. Christian does say, both in the issue and this pull request, that he doesn't really know how to uniquely identify an instance of Home Assistant. 
I'm not sure there is. 
An idea that occurs to me is that the integration has an optional parameter "name" (defaults to "Entur" IIRC), that at least some users are configuring. I have mine set to "Reise" ("Travel"). Using this value as part of the API client name should help a little.

Ah, right, I thought that a file or something that would be needed in the config was maybe missing from the pull-request.

I can look into this, but is really a per-instance identification required? Entur writes on https://developer.entur.org/pages-intro-authentication:
>  The structure of ET-Client-Name should be: "company-application".
> Header examples: "brakar-journeyplanner" ...

So wouldn't something along the lines of `homeassistant-enturplugin` be sufficient?

   -Volker

> Ah, right, I thought that a file or something that would be needed in the config was maybe missing from the pull-request.
> 
> I can look into this, but is really a per-instance identification required? Entur writes on https://developer.entur.org/pages-intro-authentication:
> 
> > The structure of ET-Client-Name should be: "company-application".
> > Header examples: "brakar-journeyplanner" ...
> 
> So wouldn't something along the lines of `homeassistant-enturplugin` be sufficient?
> 
> -Volker

Volker,

I agree with your reading of that passage. Maybe the problem is homeassistant-homeassistant, so changing it to something else like homeassistant-enturplugin may work.

That's also why I commented that maybe the plugin code is broken, so the configured string isn't getting put in the correct header.

They seem to be treating Home Assistant requests like "unidentified" requests, as if the header isn't there at all. But maybe they have a check that the two parts of the string are different.

Peter

It has to be unique. homeassistant-homeassistant will be excactly the same as homeassistant-enturplugin

Ill double check that the string is put in the correct header, but first I need a way to make the string unique per user

I checked a little bit the forums etc., it seems there's no global GUID/UUID for an instance that could be reused for this purpose. Given that Entur must be configured via `configuration.yaml` anyway, why not make the user configure a suffix there. Adding a config-item and using it in the plugin is also a well-trodden path and should be easy to do -- I could help with that if you like.

> It has to be unique. homeassistant-homeassistant will be excactly the same as homeassistant-enturplugin
> 
> Ill double check that the string is put in the correct header, but first I need a way to make the string unique per user

Yeah, I wouldn't be surprised if requests using the same client ID from a bunch of different IP-addresses triggers the rate limiting.

I'm no expert on HA, but maybe use attributes from the zone.home entity to create a more or less unique "Company" for the Client ID. friendly_name defaults to "Home", but I suspect many people change it. Or maybe a hash of latitude and longitude, perhaps prefixed by friendly_name?

E.g.:
pkv@dpen:~$ echo "10.36497923542522x63.353398562171236"|/usr/bin/md5sum
45fe2f8af37e28a70f855be661b8d068  -
Prefixed with friendly name:
Fritz Aabakkens vei 17 45fe2f8af37e28a70f855be661b8d068
Giving thsi client ID:
Fritz Aabakkens vei 17 45fe2f8af37e28a70f855be661b8d068 - Home Assistant
Or, eliminating white space:
Fritz_Aabakkens_vei_17_45fe2f8af37e28a70f855be661b8d068-HomeAssisteant

Just throwing out ideas.

- Peter

> I checked a little bit the forums etc., it seems there's no global GUID/UUID for an instance that could be reused for this purpose. Given that Entur must be configured via `configuration.yaml` anyway, why not make the user configure a suffix there. Adding a config-item and using it in the plugin is also a well-trodden path and should be easy to do -- I could help with that if you like.

Seems like a good idea, then users that want to avoid the ratelimit can add an unique suffix in the config. If you have the knowledge on how, feel free to implement. I would be grateful!

issue_context.body:
### The problem

Same as #66141

ERROR (MainThread) [enturclient.api] Error connecting to Entur, response http status code: 429 shows up frequently in my logs. In the [documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/entur_public_transport#faq---troubleshooting) I am unable to rate limit the API calls from the integration, even if the Note states: 

> Note that the underlying API is rate limited and to avoid getting your instance blocked from entur the sensor is only fetching new information every 45 seconds. It's recommended to not schedule updates more often than this.

Suggested fix: allow users to rate limit the calls from the sensor in configuration.yaml or sensor.yaml

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.1.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

NA

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

entur_public_transport

This is because the client-id is the same for every Home Assistant user: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/entur_public_transport/sensor.py#L25

I can try to implement a fix, but I dont know the proper way to identify a client in HA. Optimally this would be something like
API_CLIENT_NAME = "homeassistant-`unique-id-per-install`"

Any easy imports that I can do that fixes this? @hfurubotten

Christian says that he doesn't really know how to uniquely identify an instance of Home Assistant. 
I'm not sure there is. 
An idea that occurs to me is that the integration has an optional parameter "name" (defaults to "Entur" IIRC), that at least some users are configuring. I have mine set to "Reise" ("Travel"). Using this value as part of the API client name should help a little.

It may also be worth double checking the code to verify that API_CLIENT_NAME is going into the correct HTTP header (ET-Client-Name). The Entur docs say that _unidentified_ clients will be subjected to strict rate limitation. (https://developer.entur.org/pages-intro-authentication)

review_comments:
Context is not really a fit here. The context object is used when things trigger.
Also, according to upstream documentation, this must be in `<company>-<application>` format.

../Frenck

Thank you for the feedback. I just tried to illustrate the idea of what I want to accomplish. Upstream documentation is targeted towards public transport companies in Norway. I have spoken to the developers and they want "private" usecases like Home Assistant instances to uniquely identify per user. Do you have a tip or best practice on how to achieve that here?

Christian, did they say anything specific about what the unique identification should look like? I mean, should it be something identifiable, like an email address, or is something like a UUID OK?

Apparently, HA doesn't currently have a per-site UUID. As I suggested a couple of comments above, the zone.home entity could be used, e.g. by hashing the latitude and longitude attributes. This is assuming users set their Home Zone, which I expect most will, since it provides useful functionality.

Alternately, just require a configuration parameter, with some guidance in the documentation on what is required.
@pvarlien They are not that strict about it. If it starts with e.g. "homeassistant-" the suffix part can be set by us as we want as long as it in some way is unique for each user/instance.
